headline: Protesters storm Microsoft data center site
dek: Around 100 people entered the site near Amsterdam, per The Verge.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Site break-in
body: Around 100 people got onto the site where Microsoft is building a data center near Amsterdam, per The Verge and TecMundo.
Some of the group climbed a crane and hung signs against the company.

points.t: AI critics worry about its toll on the environment (TecMundo).
The collective Geef Tegengas helped organize (The Verge).
A sign tied Microsoft to the war in Gaza (The Verge).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: An older project
body: The complex will have three 85-meter towers, for Microsoft alone, per The Verge and TecMundo.
The plan dates to 2016, before the city's ban on new data centers through 2030 (The Verge).

stat.cap: Amsterdam bans new data centers until then

items.t: Work continues, with no end date (The Verge).
Another protest hit Dublin on Tuesday (The Verge).
US voters rejected data centers in local votes (The Verge).

caption.hook: Protesters stormed the site of a Microsoft data center near Amsterdam.
body: Per The Verge and TecMundo, around 100 people got onto the building site. Some climbed a crane and hung signs against AI and against Microsoft, tying the company to the war in Gaza. The Verge names the collective Geef Tegengas among the organizers.

The complex will have three 85-meter towers, for Microsoft alone. The plan dates to 2016, before the city's ban on new data centers through 2030, so work kept going. The Verge sees the protest as part of a wave across Europe, after another action in Dublin on Tuesday.
